Detailed method

The calculator opens at 500 g flour, 64% hydration, 1.8% salt, and 1.2% yeast. The balls fields open at 10 rolls of about 84 g. A spoon of oil or milk, if you add one, is extra and is not in the gram total. Shape rounds and proof them until they touch. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir the flour, water, salt, and yeast, then knead about 8 minutes until smooth. At 64% hydration the dough is soft and holds a ball. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 60 to 90 minutes. With 1.2% yeast it should nearly double.
  3. Divide Divide into ten pieces of about 84 g. Roll each into a smooth round.
  4. Pan Set the rounds close together in a buttered round pan, with a small gap. They should meet as they rise.
  5. Proof Cover the pan at about 24°C (75°F) for 40 to 60 minutes, until the rounds are puffy and joined along the sides.
  6. Bake Bake at 190°C (375°F) for 18 to 22 minutes, until the tops are golden and the sides are set.
  7. Cool Leave them in the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack. Pull them apart after about 15 minutes.
